findings.evidence: A grep for plan_rebase finds no caller outside landing.rs and the re-export in gh/mod.rs. findings.summary: Re-checking only on path overlap (plus any Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock) can miss a semantic break from a non-overlapping change, such as a changed function signature in a file the candidate calls.
findings.evidence: D145 and the request ask for exactly this rule, and the manifest widening plus land_pr's merged-content check reduce the risk. It is worth tracking once the share is measured live.

summary: The change adds a pure rule, rebase_needs_recheck. It asks for a re-check when a path the rebase touched overlaps a path the candidate changed (the plan's overlap rule, ignoring the shared append-only files) or is any Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock. Under the landing lock, Drain::land applies the rule before landing. The drain holds the re-check's cost cap against the budget first. A failed re-check stays owed on the retry, so a job never lands on failed checks. The drain counts every rebase that moved a branch and every one that needed a re-check, and the summary prints the share, e.g. 'rebases: 1 of 2 needed a re-check (...)'. I ran the 10 new integration tests through drain_concurrent and drain, and the 6 unit tests of the rule; all pass. They cover the overlap case, the no-overlap case, the share in the rendered summary, the failed and passing retry, the budget stop, the cost, and two workers. No existing test line was removed or edited, governance files are untouched, and Athena's CI record shows fmt, clippy and tests passing. The four changed files are all on the deliverables list. The main limitation is disclosed in the changelog and docs: the A6 drain wiring is absent, so the real steps never rebase and the share is not yet measured in a live drain. The accepted reading allows this, so it is minor.
